title: Veryfi Thinking Mode for Automation Teams in 2026
summary: Veryfi thinking mode uses reasoning-style extraction for complex documents. Find out how it differs from standard extraction and when to use each approach.
body_markdown:
## Connect Veryfi Thinking Mode in Activepieces workflows today


You can connect Thinking Mode to an Activepieces flow through three general building blocks, simplest first. Activepieces has shipped nothing specific to it as of 2026-11-20. We haven't run Thinking Mode ourselves, so each check below is yours to perform.


### Option 1: an HTTP request step


Add an HTTP request step after your trigger, for example a new attachment arriving in a mailbox, and call the Veryfi API with the settings Veryfi documents for Thinking Mode. Put the API credentials in the step's headers, not in the flow text.


Check: run the flow on one known document and confirm the response contains the fields you expect, such as vendor, date and total. If a field is empty, stop here. Nothing downstream will fix it.


Option 2 is an AI step with a model you choose. Activepieces runs any major model in an AI step, or your own provider key, so you choose the model and the spend lands on your own provider bill.


That makes it a route to a general-purpose model, not to Thinking Mode, and we haven't seen Veryfi document a model endpoint of its own. Confirm that with Veryfi before building.


Check: send a document through the step and confirm structured fields come back, not free text you must parse afterward.


### Use Veryfi Thinking Mode through an MCP server


If you want an AI agent in your flow to call Veryfi as a tool, use an MCP server.


Activepieces registers a piece once and it works both as a flow step and as a tool on its per-project MCP server, so once the Veryfi call is a piece you don't register it a second time.


The action you test in a flow is what Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent you built would call, and you can read how that works in packages/integrations in the MIT-licensed core, the same repo where the 750 integrations are counted, meaning you likely have an existing example to reference.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production. It's still the most moving parts, so try it last.


Check: have the agent process one document and compare its returned fields against the HTTP request result from Option 1. If the two disagree, trust the direct call and debug the agent layer.


Whichever you pick, run the same document set through it, then score the output against your own ground truth.
